questions.prompt: A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of rolling an even number.
questions.answer: The sample space is \(\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). The even outcomes are \(\{2,4,6\}\), so \[P(\text{even})=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}.\]

questions.prompt: A number is chosen uniformly from \(1\) to \(8\). Find the probability of choosing an odd number.
questions.answer: There are \(8\) equally likely choices. The odd choices are \(1,3,5,7\), so \[P(\text{odd})=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}.\]

questions.prompt: A number is chosen uniformly from \(1\) to \(10\). Find the probability that it is at most \(3\).
questions.answer: The favourable outcomes are \(1,2,3\), giving \(3\) outcomes out of \(10\). Hence \[P(X\le 3)=\frac{3}{10}.\]

questions.prompt: A spinner has \(12\) equal sectors labelled \(1\) to \(12\). Find the probability of landing on a multiple of \(3\).
questions.answer: The multiples of \(3\) are \(3,6,9,12\), so there are \(4\) favourable sectors. Thus \[P=\frac{4}{12}=\frac{1}{3}.\]

questions.prompt: A number is chosen uniformly from \(1\) to \(20\). Find the probability that it is prime.
questions.answer: The primes are \(2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19\), so there are \(8\) favourable outcomes. Therefore \[P=\frac{8}{20}=\frac{2}{5}.\]

questions.prompt: One card is drawn from a standard deck. Find the probability that it is a heart.
questions.answer: A standard deck has \(52\) cards and \(13\) hearts. Hence \[P(\text{heart})=\frac{13}{52}=\frac{1}{4}.\]

questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability of rolling a double.
questions.answer: There are \(36\) ordered outcomes. The doubles are \((1,1),\ldots,(6,6)\), giving \(6\) outcomes. Thus \[P(\text{double})=\frac{6}{36}=\frac{1}{6}.\]

questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum is \(7\).
A fair coin is tossed four times. Find the probability of getting at least three heads.
questions.answer: There are \(2^4=16\) equally likely strings. The favourable cases are \(4\) strings with exactly three heads and \(1\) string with four heads, so \[P=\frac{5}{16}.\]

questions.prompt: A box contains \(3\) red balls and \(2\) blue balls. Two balls are drawn in order without replacement. Find the probability of drawing red then blue.
questions.answer: There are \(5\times4=20\) ordered outcomes. Favourable outcomes choose one of \(3\) red balls first and one of \(2\) blue balls second, so \(3\times2=6\). Therefore \[P=\frac{6}{20}=\frac{3}{10}.\]

questions.prompt: In a class of \(100\) students, \(37\) study physics. Find the probability that a randomly chosen student studies physics.
questions.answer: There are \(37\) favourable students out of \(100\), so \[P(\text{physics})=\frac{37}{100}.\]

questions.prompt: A batch contains \(30\) items, of which \(9\) are defective. Find the probability that a randomly chosen item is defective.
questions.answer: The favourable outcomes are the \(9\) defective items out of \(30\). Thus \[P(\text{defective})=\frac{9}{30}=\frac{3}{10}.\]

questions.prompt: A bag contains \(15\) marbles, of which \(4\) are green. Find the probability of drawing a green marble.
questions.answer: There are \(4\) green marbles among \(15\) total marbles. Hence \[P(\text{green})=\frac{4}{15}.\]

questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed six times. Find the probability of getting six heads.
questions.answer: There are \(2^6=64\) equally likely strings, and only \(HHHHHH\) has six heads. Thus \[P(\text{six heads})=\frac{1}{64}.\]

questions.prompt: In \(90\) train journeys, \(18\) are delayed. Estimate the probability that a randomly chosen journey is delayed.
questions.answer: Using relative frequency, \[P(\text{delayed})\approx\frac{18}{90}=\frac{1}{5}=0.2.\]

questions.prompt: A test has \(40\) scripts, and \(7\) score above \(80\). Find the probability that a randomly chosen script scored above \(80\).
questions.answer: There are \(7\) favourable scripts out of \(40\), so \[P=\frac{7}{40}=0.175.\]

questions.prompt: A shop records \(120\) customers, of whom \(45\) pay by card. Find the probability that a randomly chosen customer paid by card.
questions.answer: The probability is favourable over total: \[P(\text{card})=\frac{45}{120}=\frac{3}{8}=0.375.\]

questions.prompt: In \(200\) component tests, \(3\) components fail. Estimate the probability that a component fails the test.
questions.answer: The relative frequency estimate is \[P(\text{fail})\approx\frac{3}{200}=0.015.\]

questions.prompt: A data set records \(84\) arrivals, of which \(21\) occur on weekdays. Find the probability that a randomly chosen arrival is a weekday arrival.
questions.answer: There are \(21\) weekday arrivals out of \(84\). Therefore \[P=\frac{21}{84}=\frac{1}{4}.\]

questions.prompt: A box contains cards numbered \(1\) to \(28\). Find the probability of drawing a card numbered above \(15\).
questions.answer: The numbers above \(15\) are \(16\) through \(28\), giving \(13\) cards. Hence \[P=\frac{13}{28}.\]
